pulse.text: **The Mythos ladder gave back yesterday's jump**: Polymarket's next-Mythos-class market now prices **38% for a release by Sep 1**, down from 67% at the last sweep, with Sep 2 falling to 54% from 71% and the Aug 31 leg expiring at 4%; the by-Sep-30 leg eased to **89%** from 92% on $824K of volume. Nothing has shipped since Tencent's Hy4 preview on Aug 28, so the leaderboard is untouched — **Claude Opus 5 still leads at 63** on the AA-Index over Fable 5 at 62 and a 61-point tie between Grok 4.6 and GPT-5.6 Sol. The rest of the release board barely moved: OpenAI's Astra holds **86% by Sep 30**, GPT-6 nudged up to 73% by Dec 31, and the next Gemini Pro firmed to 66% by Oct 31 from 64%. The news this sweep is all buildout politics — Axios reports an industry-funded advocacy group with **roughly $50M on hand opening data-center campaigns in Kansas, Ohio and Wisconsin**, while OpenAI says its first custom chip, Jalapeño, beat selected Nvidia systems by 1.5x to 1.9x on performance per watt. Watch Astra's Sep 15 leg at 75% — it is now the nearest dated frontier event on the board.
